ai.literal: Without moving away, without approaching, fire those-who-warm-themselves let-them-be-like, conflict kings having-joined those-who-conduct-themselves.
ai.translation: Those who associate with powerful kings should act like people warming themselves at a fire, neither moving too far away nor approaching too closely.
ai.modern: வலிமைமிக்க அரசர்களைச் சார்ந்து வாழ்பவர்கள், குளிருக்காகத் தீக்காய்வாரைப் போல அரசரை விட்டு மிகவும் விலகாமலும், மிகவும் நெருங்காமலும் அளவோடு பழக வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises those who serve or associate with kings on the proper distance to maintain. It uses the simile of warming oneself at a fire. If one gets too close to the fire, it burns; if one moves too far away, it does not provide warmth. Similarly, being too intimate with powerful rulers can be dangerous, while being too distant means losing their favor and protection.

ai.literal: kings - things desired - not desiring - by kings - enduring - wealth - will give
ai.translation: Not coveting the things that kings desire will yield enduring wealth through those very kings.
ai.modern: அரசர்கள் விரும்பும் பொருள்களைத் தான் விரும்பாமல் இருப்பது, அந்த அரசர்களாலேயே ஒருவனுக்கு நிலைபெற்ற செல்வத்தைப் பெற்றுத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises those who serve or associate with rulers on how to secure lasting prosperity. The phrase 'மன்னர் விழைப' refers to the objects, pleasures, or ambitions that the king himself desires. 'விழையாமை' means refraining from coveting those same things, as competing with a ruler leads to their displeasure and one's own ruin. By avoiding such rivalry, an associate earns the ruler's trust, which 'தரும்' (will yield) 'மன்னிய ஆக்கம்' (enduring wealth) directly 'மன்னரால்' (through the king).

ai.literal: If guarding, guarding against serious mistakes; after having suspected, convincing is difficult for anyone.
ai.translation: If you wish to protect yourself, guard against making serious mistakes. Once the ruler grows suspicious, it is difficult for anyone to restore his trust.
ai.modern: தன்னைக் காத்துக்கொள்ள விரும்பினால், அரசனுக்குச் சந்தேகம் வரும்படியான பெரிய தவறுகளைச் செய்யாமல் காத்துக்கொள்ள வேண்டும். அரசன் ஒருமுறை சந்தேகித்துவிட்டால், அதன் பின் அவனைத் தெளிவுபடுத்துவது யாருக்கும் கடினமான செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises those serving a ruler to be extremely cautious and avoid grave errors. The word 'அரியவை' refers to serious mistakes that are hard to rectify. 'கடுத்தபின்' means after the ruler has grown suspicious or angry. The couplet warns that once a ruler's trust is broken and suspicion sets in, it is nearly impossible for anyone to clear his mind and regain his confidence.

ai.literal: Whispered words and shared smiles, having suppressed, conducting oneself (is proper) great ones' presence in.
ai.translation: When in the presence of great and excellent rulers, one should conduct oneself by suppressing the urge to whisper in others' ears and share private smiles.
ai.modern: சிறந்த பெரியவர்களான அரசர்களின் அவையில் இருக்கும்போது, மற்றவர் காதில் ரகசியம் பேசுவதையும், தமக்குள் பார்த்துச் சிரிப்பதையும் தவிர்த்து நடக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on courtly etiquette when in the presence of a king or great leaders. The phrase 'செவிச்சொல்' refers to whispering secrets, and 'சேர்ந்த நகை' means sharing a private joke or smile with someone else. Doing these in a royal assembly implies disrespect or conspiracy. Therefore, one must suppress ('அவித்து') such behaviors and conduct oneself with proper decorum ('ஒழுகல்').

ai.literal: Any matter, do not eavesdrop, do not pursue; but that matter when revealed, let one listen to the secret.
ai.translation: Do not eavesdrop or pry into any matter. But when the ruler willingly reveals that matter, then listen to the secret.
ai.modern: அரசர் பேசும் எந்தவொரு செய்தியையும் ஒட்டுக்கேட்கக் கூடாது; அதைப்பற்றித் துருவிக் கேட்கவும் கூடாது. அவராகவே அந்தச் செய்தியைச் சொல்லும் போது மட்டும் அந்த இரகசியத்தைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to handle a ruler's confidential matters. The words 'ஓரார்' (do not eavesdrop) and 'தொடரார்' (do not pursue) instruct the courtier never to spy on or pry into private discussions. The couplet concludes that one should only listen to a secret ('மறை') when the ruler willingly shares it ('விட்டக்கால்'), thereby maintaining trust and proper boundaries.

ai.literal: mood having-known time having-considered dislike without desirable-things pleasingly to-speak.
ai.translation: Understanding the mood and considering the right time, one should speak desirable things that cause no offense, in a pleasing manner.
ai.modern: அரசரின் மனக்குறிப்பை அறிந்து, ஏற்ற காலத்தையும் கருதி, வெறுப்பு தராத தேவையான காரியங்களை அவர் விரும்பும் வகையில் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to speak to a ruler or a person in power. First, one must gauge their current mood ('குறிப்பு') and choose the appropriate time ('காலம்'). Then, the words spoken should be useful and desirable ('வேண்டுப'), free from anything that might cause offense ('வெறுப்பு இல'), and delivered in a way that pleases the listener ('வேட்ப'). The word 'வேட்ப' emphasizes that even necessary advice must be presented attractively.

ai.literal: Pleasing things having said, use without always even if asked not saying leave.
ai.translation: Speak what is pleasing, but never speak useless words, even if asked.
ai.modern: அரசனுக்கு விருப்பமான நல்ல செய்திகளை மட்டுமே சொல்ல வேண்டும். பயன்தராத செய்திகளை அவர் கேட்டாலும் எக்காலத்திலும் சொல்லாமல் விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on the discipline of speech required when serving a ruler. The phrase 'வேட்பன சொல்லி' means one should speak things that are pleasing and desirable. The word 'வினை' typically means action or deed, but here it takes the sense of usefulness or productive result. Thus, 'வினையில' refers to words that produce no useful outcome. The couplet emphasizes that even if the ruler explicitly asks ('கேட்பினும்'), one must refrain from speaking useless things at all times ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்').

ai.literal: "They are young", "they are relatives", saying, they will not despise; with the standing splendor, to behave is fitting.
ai.translation: One should not disrespect the ruler by thinking 'he is younger' or 'he is a relative.' Instead, one must conduct oneself in accordance with the enduring splendor of his position.
ai.modern: இவர் என்னை விட வயதில் இளையவர் என்றோ, எனக்கு உறவினர் என்றோ அரசரை அவமதிக்கக் கூடாது. மாறாக, அரசப் பதவிக்கு உரிய நிலைத்த பெருமையோடு பொருந்தி நடப்பதே முறையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on the proper decorum when serving a ruler who might be younger or related by blood. Familiarity or age differences should not lead to disrespect. The word 'ஒளி' (light or splendor) refers to the majesty and authority inherent in the ruler's position. Therefore, one must always act in accordance with that enduring royal dignity, setting aside personal familiarity.

ai.literal: "We are accepted" thus having thought, unacceptable things they will not do, those of vision without wavering.
ai.translation: Those of unwavering clear vision will not commit unacceptable acts, simply presuming "We are highly esteemed."
ai.modern: 'நாம் அரசரால் பெரிதும் மதிக்கப்படுகிறோம்' என்று எண்ணி, தகாத செயல்களைத் தெளிவான அறிவை உடையவர்கள் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the arrogance that can come from being close to power. Even if one thinks "We are highly esteemed by the ruler" (கொளப்பட்டேம் என்று எண்ணி), one must not commit inappropriate or unacceptable acts (கொள்ளாத). People of unwavering, clear judgment (துளக்கு அற்ற காட்சியவர்) understand this and never let their privileged position compromise their proper conduct.

ai.literal: Thinking 'we are old friends' and doing things that are not proper conduct, such intimacy will yield ruin.
ai.translation: Taking liberties by thinking 'we are old friends' and doing improper things will bring ruin.
ai.modern: நாம் அரசருக்குப் பழைய நண்பர்கள் என்று கருதி, பண்பற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யும் உரிமை ஒருவருக்கு அழிவையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against taking undue liberties with a ruler based on long-standing friendship. The word 'பழையம்' captures the presumption of a person who thinks their old ties grant them special privileges. When this presumed intimacy ('கெழுதகைமை') leads someone to act improperly, it will ultimately result in their own ruin. A wise person maintains respectful boundaries regardless of how long they have known the king.
